Variable.name: INTRODUCTION   You are being invited to participate in this study because you meet the criteria as a patient with Parkinson’s Disease, another neurological disease, or because you are asked to participate as a healthy control. This study aims to create an easy-to-use tool to assess the risk of a person going on to develop, or already having, Parkinson disease. Such a test would represent a valuable, clinical tool to identify at-risk individuals and forecast the course from a normal stage to a prodromal phase and on to a clinical stage.ARE THERE ANY CONFLICTS OF INTEREST?  There are no conflicts of interest to declare related to this study.   WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?Your participation in this study will require the completion of a questionnaire. The questionnaire asks questions about lifestyle, genetics and biometrics. This should take approximately 15 minutes of your time.The information you provide is for research purposes only. Some of the questions are personal.   Communication via e-mail is not absolutely secure. We do not recommend that you communicate sensitive personal information via e-mail.   As a current/past participant in this study, any new information that might affect your willingness to continue to participate in this study or, that is relevant to your previous participation must be provided to you.   The new information includes the implementation of the next step in our study, the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT- 40).  This is a non-invasive, 40 item, scratch and sniff test that provides an indication of smell loss. This will allow an accurate assessment of smell loss demonstrated to be an early indicator of Parkinson’s Disease. This should take approximately 20 minutes of your time.   VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION AND WITHDRAWAL:You do not have to be in this study if you do not want to be. You can choose to end your participation in this research (called withdrawal) at any time without having to provide a reason. The decision will not affect any healthcare services you are entitled to at The Ottawa Hospital.  If you decide to leave the study, you can ask that the information that was collected about you not be used for the study. Let the research team know if you choose this.   RISKS AND/OR BENEFITS Participation involves minimal risk to you. Some of the questions may however make you feel uncomfortable. You may not receive a direct benefit from participating in this study.  We hope the information learned from this study will help us to validate the questionnaire, which will be used in the future to help identify people at risk for Parkinson disease, or who are at an early stage of the illness. This will help at-risk individuals to be seen by a neurologist sooner to receive a diagnosis and to be enrolled in prevention/intervention trials in the future.  PRIVACY/CONFIDENTIATLITY:  Records identifying you at this centre will be kept confidential and, to the extent permitted by the applicable laws, will not be disclosed or made publicly available, except as described in this consent document.  Authorized representatives of the following organizations may look at your original (identifiable) research records at the site where these records are held, to check that the information collected for the study is correct and follows proper laws and guidelines.   	Dr. Michael Schlossmacher (Principal Investigator), Dr. Juan Li (methodologist), Kelsey Grimes, MSc (primary research staff)   	The Ottawa Health Science Network Research Ethics Board who oversees the ethical conduct of this study. 	Ottawa Hospital Research Institute to oversee the conduct of research at this location.   Information that is collected about you for the study (called study data) may also be sent to the organizations listed above. Your name, address, email, or other information that may directly identify you will not be used. The records received by these organizations may contain your Study ID number.  This research study is collecting information on race and ethnicity as well as other characteristics of individuals. Providing information on your race or ethnic origin is required as these characteristics are thought to influence your likelihood of having or developing Parkinson disease.   If the results of this study are published, your identity will remain confidential. It is expected that the information collected during this study will used in analyses and will be published/ presented to the scientific community at meetings and in journals.  Your de-identified data from this study may be used for other research purposes. If your study data is shared with other researchers, information that links your study data directly to you will not be shared. Information will be archived for 10 years after the study is complete and housed on OHRI servers.   Even though the risk of identifying you from the study data is very small, it can never be completely eliminated.  COST AND/OR PAYMENT:  You will not be paid for being in this study, nor will there be any cost to you.  RIGHTS OF PARTICIPANTS  You will be told, in a timely manner, about new information that may be relevant to your willingness to stay in this study.  You have the right to be informed of the results of this study once the entire study is complete. If you would like to be informed of the results of this study, please let the research team know.  Your rights to privacy are legally protected by federal and provincial laws that require safeguards to ensure that your privacy is respected.  QUESTIONS:If you have any questions about taking part in this study, you may contact Kelsey Grimes, Clinical Research Assistant at kgrimes@ohri.ca.  If you have questions about your rights as a participant or about ethical issues related to this study, you can talk to someone who is not involved in the study at all. Please contact The Ottawa Health Science Network Research Ethics Board, Chairperson at 613-798-5555 extension 16719.       CONSENT  By completing this questionnaire your consent to participate is implied.

Variable.name: INTRODUCTION    You are being invited to participate in this study because you meet the criteria as a patient with Parkinson’s Disease, another neurological disease, or because you are asked to participate as a healthy control. This study aims to create an easy-to-use tool to assess the risk of a person going on to develop, or already having, Parkinson disease. Such a test would represent a valuable, clinical tool to identify at-risk individuals and forecast the course from a normal stage to a prodromal phase and on to a clinical stage.  ARE THERE ANY CONFLICTS OF INTEREST?  The Neuroscent testing card was developed by our researchers and may be commercialized in the future.  WHAT WILL HAPPEN DURING THIS STUDY?  Your participation in this study will require the completion of a questionnaire. The questionnaire asks questions about lifestyleand biometrics. This should take approximately 15 minutes of your time.  The information you provide is for research purposes only. Some of the questions are personal.  Communication via e-mail is not absolutely secure. We do not recommend that you communicate sensitive personal information via e-mail.  As a current/past participant in this study, any new information that might affect your willingness to continue to participate in this study or, that is relevant to your previous participation must be provided to you.   The new information includes the implementation of the next step in our study, the Neuroscent Smell Identification Test.   This is a non-invasive, 8 item, scratch and sniff test that provides an indication of smell loss. This will allow an accurate assessment of smell loss demonstrated to be an early indicator of Parkinson’s Disease. This should take approximately 15 minutes of your time.   VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION AND WITHDRAWAL:  You do not have to be in this study if you do not want to be. You can choose to end your participation in this research (called withdrawal) at any time without having to provide a reason. The decision will not affect any healthcare services you are entitled to at The Ottawa Hospital and the Elizabeth Bruyère.   If you decide to leave the study, you can ask that the information that was collected about you not be used for the study. Let the research team know if you choose this.   RISKS AND/OR BENEFITS Participation involves minimal risk to you. Some of the questions may however make you feel uncomfortable.  You may not receive a direct benefit from participating in this study.  We hope the information learned from this study will help us to validate the questionnaire, which will be used in the future to help identify people at risk for Parkinson disease, or who are at an early stage of the illness. This will help at-risk individuals to be seen by a neurologist sooner to receive a diagnosis and to be enrolled in prevention/intervention trials in the future.  PRIVACY/CONFIDENTIATLITY:  Records identifying you at this centre will be kept confidential and, to the extent permitted by the applicable laws, will not be disclosed or made publicly available, except as described in this consent document.  Authorized representatives of the following organizations may look at your original (identifiable) research records at the site where these records are held, to check that the information collected for the study is correct and follows proper laws and guidelines.   	Dr. Michael Schlossmacher (Principal Investigator), Dr. Juan Li (methodologist), Kelsey Grimes, MSc (primary research staff)   	The Ottawa Health Science Network Research Ethics Board who oversees the ethical conduct of this study. 	Ottawa Hospital Research Institute to oversee the conduct of research at this location.   Information that is collected about you for the study (called study data) may also be sent to the organizations listed above. Your name, address, email, or other information that may directly identify you will not be used. The records received by these organizations may contain your Study ID number.  This research study is collecting information on race and ethnicity as well as other characteristics of individuals. Providing information on your race or ethnic origin is required as these characteristics are thought to influence your likelihood of having or developing Parkinson disease.  If the results of this study are published, your identity will remain confidential. It is expected that the information collected during this study will used in analyses and will be published/ presented to the scientific community at meetings and in journals.  Your de-identified data from this study may be used for other research purposes. If your study data is shared with other researchers, information that links your study data directly to you will not be shared.  Even though the risk of identifying you from the study data is very small, it can never be completely eliminated.  COST AND/OR PAYMENT:  You will not be paid for being in this study, nor will there be any cost to you.  RIGHTS OF PARTICIPANTS  You will be told, in a timely manner, about new information that may be relevant to your willingness to stay in this study.  You have the right to be informed of the results of this study once the entire study is complete. If you would like to be informed of the results of this study, please let the research team know.  Your rights to privacy are legally protected by federal and provincial laws that require safeguards to ensure that your privacy is respected.  QUESTIONS:    If you have any questions about taking part in this study, you may contact the Clinical Research Assistant at predigt.trial@ohri.ca.  If you have questions about your rights as a participant or about ethical issues related to this study, you can talk to someone who is not involved in the study at all. Please contact The Ottawa Health Science Network Research Ethics Board, Chairperson at 613-798-5555 extension 16719.  CONSENT  By completing this questionnaire your consent to participate is implied.
